To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a system that can classify histopathological breast WSIs with high accuracy.
context-aware stacked convolution networks (CNN) can achieve a high classification accuracy for breast WSIs into nonmalignant, DCIS, or IDC.
we propose a novel context-aware stacked convolution neural network for classification of breast whole-slide histopathological images and demonstrate its potential for routine breast diagnostics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for the classification of breast WS images using context-aware CNNs.
the automated analysis of WSIs and the development of an automated classification system for breast lesions.
the development of a novel CNN architecture, which is capable of learning both local and contextual information for classification of breast histopathology images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system achieves an Auc of 0.96 for the binary classification and obtains a three class accuracy of 81% for classifying WSIs into normal benign DCIS and IDC.
the proposed method is able to classify breast WSIs into three classes with an accuracy of 81%, which is comparable to the performance of human pathologists.
the proposed system is capable of classifying breast WSIs at high accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method can be used for automated classification of breast WSIS into non-malignant and malignant lesions and further, into DCIS, and Invasive Ductal Carcinoma.
the proposed system can be used as a decision support system for pathologists to improve their accuracy and efficiency.
we have developed and evaluated a system that uses context-aware stacked CNNs to classify breast WSIs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a stacked CNN architecture trained on large input patches can be used for classification of histopathology images with high accuracy.
a combination of high-resolution CNNs can be used to learn features from WSIs and improve classification performance.
the use of high-resolution CNNs and stacking of multiple networks is a promising approach for automated classification of breast WSIS.
